en: Oṃ, salutations to Vināyaka; salutations to Vighnarāja; salutations to Gaurīputra; salutations to Gaṇeśvara; salutations to Skandāgraja; salutations to the Imperishable; salutations to the Pure; salutations to the Overseer of Dakṣa; salutations to the Beloved of the Twice-born; salutations to the Divider of the Womb of Fire; salutations to the Bestower of Indra’s Fortune; salutations to the Bestower of the Strength of Speech; salutations to the Bestower of All Siddhis; salutations to the Son of Śarva; salutations to the Offspring of Gaurī; salutations to the Beloved of the Night.

Salutation to the one whose self is all things; salutation to the creator of the universe; salutation to the one worshipped by the hosts of gods; salutation to Śiva; salutation to the pure one; salutation to the beloved of wisdom; salutation to the peaceful one; salutation to the celibate student; salutation to the elephant-faced one; salutation to the son of two mothers; salutation to the one praised by sages; salutation to the destroyer of obstacles for devotees; salutation to the one with a single tusk; salutation to the four-armed one; salutation to the one endowed with power (Śakti); salutation to the clever one; salutation to the long-bellied one.

Salutations to Śūrpakarṇa; salutations to Heraṃba; salutations to the supreme knower of Brahman; salutations to Kāla; salutations to the Lord of the planets; salutations to the lover; salutations to the one whose eyes are the Moon, the Sun, and Fire; salutations to the bearer of the noose and the goad; salutations to the Vedic meter; salutations to the one who has transcended the qualities (guṇas); salutations to the stainless one; salutations to the one free from blemish; salutations to the one whose feet are worshipped by those who have attained self-perfection; salutations to the one who holds a citron fruit in his hand; salutations to the unmanifest; salutations to the wielder of the mace; salutations to the giver of boons; salutations to the eternal one.

Salutations to the Accomplished One; salutations to the Beloved of the Wise; salutations to Him who is Free from Fear; salutations to the Wielder of the Discus; salutations to the Bearer of the Sugarcane Bow; salutations to Him whose hands hold the Lotus and the Blue Water-lily; salutations to the Bestower of Prosperity; salutations to the Cause of Prosperity; salutations to Him who rejoices in praise; salutations to the Possessor of the Arts; salutations to the One with Matted Hair; salutations to the Moon-Crested One; salutations to the Lord of the Immortals; salutations to Him who has a Serpent as His Sacred Thread; salutations to the Beloved of Śrī; salutations to Him whose feet are worshipped by Rāma; salutations to the One who wears a Girdle; salutations to the One of Massive Splendor.

Salutations to the creator of the three Vedas; salutations to the one who loves the sacred sound; salutations to the Supreme Person; salutations to the one with the thick trunk; salutations to the first-born; salutations to the leader; salutations to the protector of the hosts; salutations to the steadfast one; salutations to the bestower of growth; salutations to the fortunate one; salutations to the hero; salutations to the lord of speech; salutations to the bestower of success; salutations to the one fond of *dūrvā* grass and *bilva* leaves; salutations to the beloved; salutations to the remover of sins; salutations to the one by whom the scriptures were composed; salutations to the composed one; salutations to the one with the curved trunk.

Salutations to the bestower of prosperity; salutations to the gentle one; salutations to the giver of what is desired by devotees; salutations to the infallible one; salutations to the absolute one; salutations to the perfected one; salutations to the embodiment of existence, consciousness, and bliss; salutations to the wise one; salutations to the one endowed with *māyā*; salutations to the one who possesses teeth; salutations to the most devoted to Brahman; salutations to the one worshipped even by fear; salutations to the giver of fear to the intoxicated *daityas*; salutations to the one whose form is manifest; salutations to the formless one; salutations to the one who delights in the playful pastimes and caresses on the lap of Pārvatī and Śaṅkara.

Salutations to the support of the entire world; salutations to the one whose vehicle is a choice mouse; salutations to the one praised by the joyful; salutations to the one of serene soul; salutations to the bestower of all spiritual perfections. Thus ends the "Hymn of One Hundred and Eight Names of Śrī Siddhivināyaka."
